extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors considering submitting data-centric machine learning manuscripts, and reviewers/action editors for DMLR
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for submitting and reviewing manuscripts to the Journal of Data-centric Machine Learning Research (DMLR), a single-blind, OpenReview-hosted journal focused on the data aspects of ML. Covers scope, required disclosures, review procedure, and publication policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance Criteria (scope, completeness, compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Editor-in-Chief will assign an Action Editor to assess whether the submission aligns with the Acceptance Criteria, including scope, completeness, and compliance with the DMLR standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EIC may reject the submission outright before AE assignment in certain cases. Authors and reviewers should consult the Submission page, Reviewer Guidelines, and Action Editor Guidelines for detailed definitions of scope and the DMLR standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: focus on data aspect of machine learning research
rubrics_metrics.description: DMLR aims to provide a venue for high-quality scholarly articles focused on the data aspect of machine learning research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be aligned with the data-centric ML focus; authors are recommended to read the Submission page to ensure appropriateness of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-blind review / non-anonymized authors
rubrics_metrics.description: DMLR employs a single-blind review system in which authors' identities are not anonymized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy is because data work often includes the hosting of data, which usually cannot be anonymized. Authors must create author profiles on OpenReview and disclose potential conflicts of interest when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory disclosures (IRB, funding, competing interests, conflicts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to provide information concerning human subjects reporting (IRB), funding, competing interests, and any conflicts not covered in their institutional history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of potential conflicts of interest is required at submission via OpenReview author profiles; ensure all relevant human-subjects approvals and funding statements are included as part of completeness/compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process structure and reviewer count
rubrics_metrics.description: If the AE opts to proceed with review, three reviewers will be recruited to evaluate and provide feedback on the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an open-ended phase for rebuttals, discussions, and revisions enabling authors to engage with reviewers and refine their paper. The AE makes the final decision informed by reviewers and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision outcomes and resubmission option
rubrics_metrics.description: AE decision options may be to accept the submission as is, accept it with minor revisions, or reject it (with an option to make revisions and resubmit it anew).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejected submissions may be revised and resubmitted as a new submission; accepted submissions become public on OpenReview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication / public availability policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions will be public on OpenReview only when they are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until acceptance, submissions remain non-public on OpenReview; authors should be aware of this policy when preparing and submitting their manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial quality bar and board composition
rubrics_metrics.description: DMLR aims to maintain the high-quality bar of JMLR with a rigorous review process and a high-profile, dedicated editorial board and review board with diverse expertise and representation from all adjacent fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal will continue to refine and tailor its process to serve data-centric ML research and hopes to be a venue for innovations tailored to this subfield; authors should expect rigorous standards similar to JMLR/TMLR.
